notes:
Account snapshot: Penumbra is a regulated finserv analytics vendor building a customer-facing recommender & remediation assistant. They've been self-hosting models but want predictable economics + SLAs for production. Interested primarily in Redwood Dedicated with VPC control and optional private control plane.

Discovery highlights (shorthand):
- Wants throughput guarantees for peak trading windows (market open/close). target: 150-250 RPS for short chat/rerank endpoints; 400k tokens/min sustained across fleet.
- Latency SLOs: P95 <120ms for 32-token replies on low-latency path; P99 SLA target 200ms for priority tier. willing to separate tiers (premium vs background).
- Model preferences: evaluating Llama-3-70B-family and Mistral-70B-advanced; open to 13B/7B for cheaper paths.
- Context requirements: two tracks — short context (<= 2k tokens) low-latency route, long context (up to 32k tokens) for litigation/records search. need KV cache strategy for long-context sessions.
- Quantization: cost sensitivity -> prefer int8 (q8-type) baseline; will test aggressive q4-style profiles for 70B if quality tolerable. Concern re: hallucination/regression when aggressive quantization used.
- HW preference: prefer H100-class for FP16/large-model throughput; acceptable A100 for quantized 70B. Planning initial reserved pool of 6-10 H100-equivalent GPUs with burst pool of 2-4 devices.
- Autoscaling & reserved: want hard reserved capacity for guaranteed throughput + ability to burst to lower-cost shared capacity.
- SLA asks: 99.95% uptime, credits tied to both availability and latency SLOs; require rollback/fallback policy in SLA for model regressions.

Quotes / call snippets:
- "We need predictable tail latency during market opens — losing seconds costs real dollars." — Head of Platform
- "If you can show steady P95 numbers with 70B quantized on H100 and a clear capacity plan, procurement will sign faster." — CTO

POC focus and success criteria:
- Baseline perf run: model vs model (70B fp16 vs 70B q8 vs 13B q4) on 1:1 HW (H100) — measure latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization. target: P95 <120ms on short route for 70B q8.
- KV cache + batching test: simulate 4k concurrent sessions with 60% reuse prefix to validate cache hit reductions in token compute. target: 35-45% token cost reduction with cache enabled.
- Throughput soak: 24hr stress at 80% of planned reserved capacity to confirm thermal/stability and autoscaling triggers.
- Regression/QA: run 3 eval prompt-sets (LLM perf, hallucination, safety) pre/post quantization; quality drop must be <1.5% relative to fp16 baseline (customer threshold).

Negotiation notes:
- Pricing ask: committed monthly reserved capacity + overage at discounted shared rate. They prefer a blended price for H100-equivalent capacity.
- SLAs: want explicit latency SLA (P95/P99 tiers) + SLO credits tied to measurable telemetry. Legal wants data residency guarantees for EU and US clients.

Internal AE/SE notes:
- SE to build two capacity plans: conservative (8 H100, no burst), mid (6 reserved + 3 burst) and aggressive (10 reserved + 4 burst). include cost models.
- Need Redwood Optimize recommendations: quant profiles to test (q8_0, q4a, q4f variants), batching window tradeoffs, and KV eviction policy tuning.

Next steps (short):
- 2026-03-17: HW sizing call (Marco + infra architect + Penumbra ops).
- Deliver capacity plan + cost model v1 by 2026-03-20.
- Run initial perf baseline week of 2026-03-24 (Marco + infra).
- Draft SLA to legal by 2026-03-31.
